analysis:
Examined the inference excerpt, test-document metadata, complete supplied test patch and base context against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. No concrete regression is established by this documentation evidence. docs/developer/test.md head 117–143 describes GLM logprob capture without speculation and replacement of redundant weight-hash passes with the verified manifest aggregate; head 197–224 describes returned-reasoning replay and buffered JSON/forced-tool validation, explicitly distinguishing scripted tests from real-model qualification. File modes are unchanged. docs/architecture/inference.md 2406–2602 describes Flint admission, bounded stop matching, reasoning/logprob withholding, tool post-validation and paged-only execution; these lines are outside its reported changed ranges. Its 2641–2647 GLM fail-closed parser and content-free shutdown diagnostic are also unchanged context, not new controls.
Integration must inspect the actual GLM loader, ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and VerifiedWeightHashStore: the orientation patch at inference.md head 684–691 states that registration can reuse a digest based on file identity metadata, while serving re-verifies. Confirm store integrity, full-manifest coverage, construction-time mutation checks, and that registration/routing or SSD cache bindings cannot treat a cached digest as verified loaded weights (T-012, T-027, T-041). Also verify GLM logprob/reasoning channel isolation and that invalid JSON or forced-tool output cannot escape through HTTP or coordinator streaming before validation (A-001, T-007, T-008, TB-007). The supplied documents do not establish those implementation contracts, test execution, or platform prompt/capability parity. Remaining inference changes, including video sampling and capability handling, are not fully visible here; this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety or a missing control.
